title: Vectors
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Vectors.

concepts.def: Quantity with magnitude and direction. Written as column or i-j form: a = (3, 4) or 3i + 4j.
|a| = √(x² + y²) for a = xi + yj. Distance in Pythagorean form.
Vector of length 1 in direction of a: â = a/|a|. Used to specify direction without magnitude.
Add component-wise: (a, b) + (c, d) = (a + c, b + d). Geometrically: tip-to-tail or parallelogram rule.
k·(x, y) = (kx, ky). Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other.
Position of point P relative to origin O written as OP. AB = OB − OA gives displacement from A to B.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Vectors — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Vectors brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Vectors.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
options: The magnitude is 7 — you add the components.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
How long the line is on the page.
5 — using sqrt(3^2 + 4^2).

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.
It means the vectors are parallel.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.

mcqs.q: What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
How long the line is on the page.
It means the vectors are parallel.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.
